start.description: start date for the data point

outlierCode.description:
outlierCode: 0 or no value -- regular point
             1 -- to be ignored when returning results of value outlier analysis
             2 -- is an estimated value
             3 -- combination of 1 and 2 together

enum (0, 1, 2)

comments.description: (Optional) any comments for the data point

isEstimated.description: Denotes if the value is an actual value or an estimated value. default = null (actual value)

dataVersion.description:
Same data points can have different data version to denote priority. Default behavior in case of overlapping
data points is to pick the data point with the highest data version.
If data version is not specified, then default (avg) overlap handling is applied to the overalapping data points

statusCode.description: Customer specific status code for the data point (may be used to denote data quality)

typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

forecastTimestamp.description:
The timestamp for which the forecast is generated.
This field records the specific time period when the forecast is valid.
It is important to know when a forecast was generated to track the evolution
of the predictions over time, especially in time-sensitive applications such as
predictive maintenance or reliability analysis.

contribution.description:
Represents the contribution value of the forecast, typically a numerical value
indicating how much a particular factor or variable contributes to the forecasted outcome.
The contribution value is essential for understanding how individual features or
components impact the forecast. For example, this could represent how a specific
environmental condition, asset usage, or operational parameter contributes to the
time-to-event prediction.
`@ts(treatmentPath='parent.treatment')` - Ensures that any transformations or adjustments
to the treatment value in the parent entity are reflected in this contribution value.

contributionUpperBound.description:
The upper bound for the contribution value. This defines the maximum possible contribution
from the feature or variable, setting a threshold that ensures the contribution does not exceed
a certain level in the forecast model.
This field helps track the upper limit of each factor's impact and provides a range within which
the contribution value can vary. It can be useful for validation and for understanding the model's
confidence in the predicted outcome.

contributionLowerBound.description:
The lower bound for the contribution value. This defines the minimum possible contribution
that a feature or variable can have in the forecast. It sets a threshold to prevent contributions
from being too low and outside the expected range for model accuracy.
This lower bound provides further validation by ensuring that contributions do not fall
below a certain threshold, thus maintaining consistency and stability in the forecasted values.

title:
Represents the contribution of individual factors or variables to a forecasted value in the context of
reliability and time-to-event (TTE) predictions. This entity captures the contribution of different
features or components for the forecasted value, along with upper and lower bounds to track the uncertainty
or range for each contribution.

The `ReliabilityTteForecastContribution` entity is used to understand and track how each variable contributes
to the model's forecast, which is essential for reliability engineering, predictive maintenance, and risk analysis.
The entity also records the timestamp for which the forecast is valid, ensuring that the contributions are linked
to specific forecast periods.

For more details on each field, refer to the documentation below.
name: ReliabilityTteForecastContribution
